description: Multimeter, plug-in jumpers, insulated wire, soldering tools and heat-shrink for PoC
notes: Both configurations use a 64-row solderless breadboard and suitable plug-in jumpers, plus a suitably rated insulated wire soldered directly from J0 pin 1 to strip +. Disconnect all power and remove the jack from the breadboard before soldering; insulate the joint and strain-relieve the wire. Verify polarity and check for shorts before energizing. Both layouts link the left/right +12 V rails and ground rails at the top and bridge all four midpoint breaks. Nano VIN connects at a15 to L+15; minimum Nano GND connects at j12 to R-12. Strip + bypasses those rails. Nano VIN and best-practice driver supply branches remain on the breadboard.

description: 12 V common-positive RGB strip; planned 160 inches total
notes: Both configurations: start with one marked cut segment; maximum 25 cm gives 3.6 W/0.30 A at full white, approximately 0.10 A per color, plus controller draw. Verify actual current; cut only at marked pads. Strip + connects directly to J0 pin 1 via a soldered insulated wire; row 40 is unused. Best-practice strip leads: a41 green, a42 red, a43 blue. Minimum exposes the same color nets on J1/J2: pin 3 red, pin 4 green, pin 5 blue; pin 2 positive connects through soldered pigtails to J0.1. Return current still passes through breadboard contacts; the positive bypass does not increase the load limit. Full 160 inches=4.064 m/58.52 W/4.88 A is for later rated wiring; minimum TN0702N3-G MOSFETs are only for the short test load. Sections connect in parallel to like pads.

description: Breadboard-friendly 2.1 mm DC barrel jack; thin-pin type
notes: Both configurations retain J0; replaces panel-mount jack for PoC. DigiKey CP-102AH-ND; CAD 1.15 checked 2026-10-16, before tax/shipping. Included in generated min.csv. Manufacturer specifies breadboard-friendly pins: https://www.adafruit.com/product/373 . Centre positive pin 1 at b58; sleeve ground pin 2 at b60; switched contact pin 3 at d59 unused. Solder the strip-positive wire to the actual pin 1 terminal, not a breadboard hole such as a58 or e58. Insulate and strain-relieve the joint; remove the jack from the breadboard before soldering. Gently form pins if needed; verify contact identity with unplugged meter. Drawing: https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/datasheets/21mmdcjackDatasheet.pdf

description: Best-practice and minimum short-strip prototypes with direct strip-positive wiring
notes: Both retain J0 and parallel Nano VIN/strip supply branches. Strip + is soldered directly to J0 pin 1, bypassing positive breadboard contacts; strip returns still use breadboard contacts. Row 40 is unused. The load limit remains 25 cm/0.30 A total. Best practice uses IRFZ44NPBF MOSFETs, two TC4427A drivers, and supporting passives. Minimum uses three TN0702N3-G MOSFETs with direct Nano gate drive and two parallel RJ-11 strip jacks J1/J2; no drivers, resistors, or capacitors. No F0/F1 holders or external J12 block in either PoC. Start with one strip segment, up to 25 cm after checking current. Full strip at low PWM brightness still has high-current pulses; do not use that as a substitute for a short load.
